title: Local finite Tor dimension is globally bounded on a quasi-compact scheme
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], with chosen derived localizations for module sheaves on $X$ and its open subschemes [def-pc-derived-category]. Let $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$. If $E$ locally has finite Tor dimension [def-pc-locally-finite-tor-dimension], then $E$ has finite Tor dimension [def-pc-finite-tor-dimension]: there exist integers $a\leq b$ such that $H^i(E\otimes^L G)=0$ for every module sheaf $G$ and every $i\notin[a,b]$. No quasi-separatedness is assumed.

source.place: Tag 08CG (definition-tor-amplitude); Tag 09U9 (lemma-tor-amplitude-stalk), proof and finite-subcover consequence

proof.text: Choose a neighbourhood U_x and interval [a_x,b_x] at each point using [def-pc-locally-finite-tor-dimension]. Compactness gives a finite set of these neighbourhoods covering X (Mathlib IsCompact.elim_finite_subcover). Insert 0 into each finite set of endpoints and take its minimum lower endpoint lo and maximum upper endpoint hi. Then lo <= 0 <= hi, lo <= a_x and b_x <= hi for every chosen neighbourhood. This also handles the empty finite cover without a separate nonemptiness assumption.

At every point select a member of the finite subcover. If i < lo or hi < i, then i < a_x or b_x < i, so its local vanishing hypothesis holds. Apply [lem-pc-tor-amplitude-open-local] with [lo,hi]. This proves [def-pc-finite-tor-dimension].

proof_origin.place: Tag 09U9 proof; the compact case also uses the finite-subcover argument in lem-pc-perfect-affine-module-preimage step 2
